articles.text: MĚIGUÓ YÓUKÈ: Dà shīfu, mángzhe na?
AMERICAN TOURIST: You must be very busy, chef.
DÀ SHĪFU: Bù máng, bù máng, jìnlai zuò, wǒ gěi nǐmen chǎole liǎngge xiǎo cài, qǐng nǐmen chángchang.
CHEF: No, no, come in and sit down. I made a couple of little stir-fried dishes for you. Please try them.
MĚIGUÓ YÓUKÈ: Wǒmen zài lìngwài yíge shítáng chīguo fàn le, chīde hǎo bǎo.
AMERICAN TOURIST: We've already eaten in another dining hall. We're very full.
DÀ SHĪFU: Zài bǎo yě děi chángchang, zhèi shi tángcùde, wǒ zhīdao nǐmen xǐhuan chī.
CHEF: No matter how full you are you must try them. This one is sweet and sour, I know you people like that.
MĚIGUÓ YÓUKÈ: Wǒ jìde wǒ zài nǎr chīguo, duì le, shi zài Huáshèngdùnde yíge Zhōngguó fànguǎnrli, měicì qù wǒ dōu qǐng tāmen zuò zhèige.
AMERICAN TOURIST: I remember having this somewhere. Oh yes, it was in a Chinese restaurant in Washington. Whenever I went there I used to ask them to make this.
DÀ SHĪFU: Xǐhuan chī jiù bǎ ta dōu chīle ba! Nǐ gāngcái shuōde nèige fànguǎnr shi Shànghǎi fànguǎnr ma?
CHEF: If you like it, then eat it all! Is the restaurant you just mentioned a Shànghǎi-style restaurant?
MĚIGUÓ YÓUKÈ: Shì.
AMERICAN TOURIST: Yes.
MĚIGUÓ YÓUKÈ: Hòulái wǒ líkāi dōngbù jiù zài yě méi chīguo nàme hǎochīde cài le.
AMERICAN TOURIST: Later I left the east and never had such delicious food again.
DÀ SHĪFU: Lái, bǎ ta dōu xiāomièle, wǎnshang wǒ zài gěi nǐmen zuò biéde.
CHEF: Come on, polish it off. Tonight I'll make you some other things.
MĚIGUÓ YÓUKÈ: Xièxie nín, dà shīfu. Nín bú shi zhèrde rén ba?
AMERICAN TOURIST: Thank you. Chef, you're not from this area, are you?
DÀ SHĪFU: Bú shì, wǒ shi Wúxī rén.
CHEF: No, I'm from Wúxī.
MĚIGUÓ YÓUKÈ: Zài Chángjiāng yǐběi?
AMERICAN TOURIST: North of the Yangtze River?
DÀ SHĪFU: Ōu, nǐ gǎocuò le, Chángjiāng yǐnán!
CHEF: Oh, you've got it wrong, south of the Yangtze!
MĚIGUÓ YÓUKÈ: Wǒ fāxiàn Jiāngnán rén xǐhuan tiánde hé làde.
AMERICAN TOURIST: I notice that people from Jiāngnán (the area south of the lower reaches of the Yangtze) like sweet foods and hot foods.
DÀ SHĪFU: Zhè dào shi duìde. Wǒmen Jiāngnán rén zuò cài bú shi tiánde jiù shi làde.
CHEF: That's true enough. When we people from Jiāngnán cook, if it isn't sweet then it's hot.
MĚIGUÓ YÓUKÈ: Nǐmen shítáng měitian yòng zhème duō cài, dōu shi cóng fùjìn gōngshè mǎide ma?
AMERICAN TOURIST: You use so much food here in your dining hall, do you buy it all from the neighboring communes?

DÀ SHĪFU: Nǎli?! Wénhuà Dà Gémìng yǐqián wǒmen zhèige zhìzàochǎng hé biéde dà chǎng yíyàng, dōu yǒu zìjǐde nóngchǎng, càidì shénmede. Dà shítáng chīde cài bú yòng shuō le, jiù shi yòu'éryuán háizimen chīde shuǐguǒ shénmede yě dōu shi zìjǐ zhòngde.

CHEF: Oh, no! Before the Cultural Revolution our factory had its own farm, vegetable plots, and so on, as other large factories did. Of course, we grew the food used in the large dining halls, but we even grew all the fruits and things the children in the kindergartens ate.
MĚIGUÓ YÓUKÈ: Hòulái ne?
AMERICAN TOURIST: And then?
DÀ SHĪFU: Hòulái, Wénhuà Dà Gémìng le, nóngchǎng, càidì dōu bèi gǎode luànqībāzāo, chīde dōngxi zhēn jǐnzhāng, yú a, ròude bú yòng shuō le, lián cài dōu bú gòu chī le.
CHEF: Then it was the Cultural Revolution, and the farm and vegetable plots were ruined. Food was in very short supply. Fish and meats were of course tight, but there weren't even enough vegetables.
MĚIGUÓ YÓUKÈ: Xiànzài hǎo le.
AMERICAN TOURIST: Now it's better.

DÀ SHĪFU: Yī Jiǔ Qī Qī nián, chǎng lǐngdǎo hàozhào quánchǎng gōngren gǎihǎo shēnghuó, nóngchǎng a, yúchǎng a, yòu gǎnqilai le, qíngxing jiù hǎoduō le. Nǐ kàn, zhème duō cài, chàbuduō dōu shi zìjǐ shēngchǎnde, yòu piányi yòu xīnxian, duō hǎo!

CHEF: In 1977, the factory leadership appealed to all the factory's workers to improve daily living conditions. We started the farm and the fishery again, and things were much better. See all these vegetables, we produced almost all of them ourselves. They're inexpensive, and fresh, too. What could be better!
MĚIGUÓ YÓUKÈ: Shíjiān bù zǎo le, àn jìhua wǒmen hái děi qù cānguān yìliǎngge dìfang ne!
AMERICAN TOURIST: It's getting late, and according to our schedule we're supposed to visit another couple of places!
DÀ SHĪFU: Hǎo, huí tóur jiàn.
CHEF: All right. See you later.
MĚIGUÓ YÓUKÈ: Huí tóur jiàn.
AMERICAN TOURIST: See you later.
